question: Which of the following organisms is commonly referred to as bread mould?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rhizopus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rhizopus** is a genus of common saprophytic fungi.
 
• They are also known as **bread moulds** because they commonly grow on bread.
 
• These fungi belong to the class **Zygomycetes** and are found in different environments.
 
• Rhizopus species can also grow on a variety of other organic materials, including fruits and vegetables.
 
• They reproduce through the formation of spores, which are produced in a structure called a **sporangium**.
 
• Rhizopus plays an important role in the decomposition of organic matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Yeast**__

 __
 
• **Yeast** is a type of fungus that is used in baking and brewing.
 
• They are single-celled microorganisms that can ferment sugars, producing carbon dioxide and alcohol.
 
• Yeasts are not typically referred to as bread moulds, although they are essential for bread making.
 
 
 
• **Planaria**__
 __
 
• **Planaria** are flatworms belonging to the class **Turbellaria**.
 
• They are known for their ability to regenerate lost body parts.
 
• Planaria are not fungi and do not grow on bread.
 
 
 
• **Spirogyra**__
 
 
• **Spirogyra** is a genus of filamentous green algae.
 
• They are commonly found in freshwater environments such as ponds and streams.
 
• Spirogyra is not related to bread moulds and does not grow on bread.
